rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -E '\britual|\bceremony' → 0 matches in body (lines 1-83)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is pre-arc, so the M1 vocabulary bar is at its floor; terms used (plan mode, rules and memory, gh, PR) are either assumed-known or plainly described, none pull forward a later-module coinage

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No forcing function moved from body into a fenced prompt this cycle

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The What happened: block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is not an exercise; no What happened: block present or expected

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Agent-directed verbs stay peer-flat throughout: 'Ask Claude to fetch' (line 45), 'push back if it dumps' (line 62), 'ask Claude to use' (line 66)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section headers ('Bring real work', 'Pick THE repo', 'Open a Claude Code session in that repo', 'Get the content folder onto your laptop', 'Extract the bundle and install the curated skills', 'Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') are literally accurate to what each section does; no spatial-metaphor or unnamed-'other' faults

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negation, deictic drumroll, bold-label echo, or citation duplication in body; closest candidate is line 82's 'Doesn't have to be big', which negates against a real prior claim (the trick request) rather than an unguessed one

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 13 lede 'Roughly in the order you'll reach for them:' already states the ordering; line 16's per-item marker 'A small multi-file task, soon after' is a pure positional marker (names only where the item sits, no independent constraint) — this is the exact banned example the rule itself quotes ('for the back half, later on, soon after'). Line 15's 'wanted on day one' survives the carve-out (a real deadline: the one item that must be picked before arrival); 'soon after' does not.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut ', soon after' from line 16 — the lede already carries the ordering

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No superlative slogan (only/always/never/nothing else/the one thing that) in body prose to test

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only one backed claim in the file (Willison pre-read, source-verification block); no sibling file re-states this claim's body text within scope

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single-file re-fire, not a multi-file sweep

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No tier-pegging or corrective-gap phrasing ('at your scale', 'a senior would already know') in body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is pre-M2 so bare 'M1' abbreviation rule doesn't license shortcuts here, and body correctly uses full 'Module 1' throughout (lines 7, 58, 76, 78, 80, 82); assumed-known terms (PR, repo, gh, GitHub CLI) are industry-standard for this audience per the assumed-known carve-out

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No unearned-tech-word flinch terms for this engineer audience; AE101 files carry the assumed-known carve-out for MCP/CI/PR-class vocabulary anyway

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always you, never the student; teacher framing stays out of body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The flagged arc-narration sentence ('Every module of this training starts from a Claude Code session in this repo.') is confirmed deleted. A sibling survives at line 11: 'The training runs on YOUR real work.' — subject is 'The training', not the student's repo/task/artifact. Deletion test: cutting it leaves 'You'll work at different task sizes across the training, bring something at each size from your backlog.' reading cleanly, and the header '## Bring real work' (line 9) already carries the same fact. Not a canonical signposting section (not What You'll Learn/Connections/Bridge/Prework/The point), so no exemption applies.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut line 11's first sentence; the header and the next sentence already carry the premise
